transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-18 15:00 UTC
- Duration: 48 minutes
- Attendees: Jordan Ellis (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Dr. Maya Chen, Ravi Patel, Elena Gomez, Samir Nair (Centauri Medical)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on Private deployment networking: VPC peering, private endpoints, regional restrictions for PHI workloads, egress IPs, and compliance requirements. Next steps: share network guide, schedule deep-dive, and provide pricing.

Transcript:
00:00 Jordan Ellis: hey everyone thanks for joining; i'm jordan from redwood inference, i run the east accounts here, um today with priya our solutions engineer. quick intro?
00:12 Dr. Maya Chen: hi maya here, head of platform at centauri medical; we run patient-facing models and are evaluating redwood for private vpc/deployed inference, lots of PHI concerns.
00:21 Ravi Patel: ravi, infra lead. we're primarily on aws in us-east-1 and us-west-2, we use transit gateways and have pretty strict egress controls.
00:30 Priya Nair: thanks, hi all. quick agenda: understand your network topology, constraints (regions, peering options), KMS/HSM needs, and success criteria for a pilot.
00:45 Elena Gomez: and i'll be watching for compliance stuff - audit logs, key management, data residency.
00:52 Jordan Ellis: great. first question - are you leaning private vpc or dedicated hosted? i know you mentioned private earlier.
01:00 Dr. Maya Chen: private vpc. We need the inference plane inside our VPC or peered private network because of PHI, and we need audit trails. latency also matters for near-real-time triage.
01:12 Jordan Ellis: understood. to clarify, our "Redwood Private" deploy can run in your VPC via peering or via private endpoints depending on cloud. we do both models: vpc peering (direct routing) or private endpoint / interface endpoint, similar to aws privatelink. each has tradeoffs.
01:30 Ravi Patel: can you explain the tradeoffs - we use Transit Gateway and cross-account peering is limited.
01:36 Priya Nair: sure. vpc peering is L3 routing - simpler latency, but doesn't scale well for many VPCs and doesn't traverse TGW in some configs. private endpoints (like aws interface endpoints/privatelink) give you granular control per service and cross-account access with enforced endpoint policies and simpler egress control. for high throughput low-latency inference, peering sometimes gives better p99 latency because there's no reverse-proxy hop, but privatelink gives better security posture in complex orgs.
02:05 Ravi Patel: ok. we also have strict egress requirements - all outbound must come from fixed elastic NAT IPs for partner allow-lists. can redwood support fixed egress IPs from the inference nodes?
02:18 Priya Nair: yes - in our private deployment we can announce egress from a set of static IPs, typically via a NAT/egress gateway appliance in the customer's environment or via our managed egress IPs when peering. we will share the egress IP range and port matrix. note: if you use privatelink, outbound to 3rd parties still follows your VPC routing.
02:38 Samir Nair: do you require inbound ports open to the model hosts? our security team is sensitive to any inbound rules.
02:45 Jordan Ellis: inbound ports - typically we ask for TCP 443 to reach the private endpoint if using interface endpoints. for peering, traffic is initiated from customer to our service so minimal inbound rules, but we'll provide an explicit port matrix (we referenced this as private-deploy-guide.pdf).
03:00 Elena Gomez: what about cross-region constraints? we have PHI that must remain in us-east-1 for certain datasets. can the private deployment be pinned to a single region?
03:10 Priya Nair: yes - you can pin model serving to a specific region/availability zone. Redwood supports region pinning for Private deployments and Dedicated pools. If you need multi-region failover, we can do active-passive with async replication of model artifacts, but you'll need to accept cross-region replication if you want warm failover unless we keep entirely separate models per region.
03:34 Ravi Patel: replication for model weights - does that imply egress of artifacts out of your VPC? for compliance we need to audit every transfer.
03:41 Jordan Ellis: correct - model artifacts can be stored in your S3 and we can pull them into the serving cluster in region. we log all transfers and can provide audit entries; we'll include that in the SOC2 docs.
03:55 Dr. Maya Chen: KMS - we use AWS KMS with customer-managed keys, HSM-backed. do you integrate with CMKs?
04:03 Priya Nair: yes - we support KMS integrations. For Private, you can provide access to your KMS via a cross-account role or we can integrate with bring-your-own-HSM in supported setups. we have customers using CMKs for token encryption and we can surface logs.
04:18 Elena Gomez: audit log retention - what's the default and can we forward logs to our SIEM?
04:24 Jordan Ellis: default retention in Redwood Console is 90 days for detailed traces, but for enterprise/private we can extend retention and forward to your S3/CloudWatch/LogRhythm via secure transfer. we'll capture request/response metadata but by default we redact prompt content for privacy unless you opt-in.
04:44 Ravi Patel: latency SLOs - what's realistic? we need sub-200ms p95 for short prompts (<=512 tokens).
04:51 Priya Nair: on-prem/peered private deployments with pinned models in the same AZ typically achieve ~60-120ms p95 for small models; larger generation workloads will be higher. Dedicated pools give consistent throughput; if you need strict SLOs we recommend Dedicated with reserved capacity or colocated Private nodes. we'll share recent benchmarks from similar customers (attached: benchmark-sheet.csv).
05:18 Dr. Maya Chen: firewall rules - can you provide exact CIDR ranges? we need them to open to our perimeter firewall.
05:24 Jordan Ellis: yes - action: we'll share CIDR + egress ports. typical ports: 443 outbound, some internal health probes between infra nodes - all documented in the guide.
05:33 Samir Nair: what about network MTU and jumbo frames? we use 9001 in some clusters.
05:38 Priya Nair: our runtime is tolerant but we recommend default MTU 1500 for public cloud peering; jumbo frames can introduce fragmentation across different network devices. we'll note guidance.
05:50 Ravi Patel: on routing - does redwood require BGP or static routes for peering with TGW?
05:56 Priya Nair: we can support both. For high-throughput low-latency setups, customers prefer static route peering; for dynamic failover setups we can support BGP through a managed appliance. we'll map both options in the network guide.
06:12 Elena Gomez: compliance - do you have SOC2, ISO 27001? and do you support SSO/SAML with SCIM provisioning?
06:20 Jordan Ellis: yes - Redwood is SOC2 Type II and ISO27001 certified; we support SSO/SAML and SCIM. for Private deployments we can also do customer-managed identity with on-prem connectors. we'll attach the compliance kit.
06:34 Dr. Maya Chen: are there any features that don't work inside Private? e.g., streaming or function calling?
06:41 Priya Nair: streaming works over private endpoints; function/tool calling is supported but requires additional config for outbound tool webhooks - you'll need to allow those outbound flows or configure a webhook proxy inside your VPC.
06:55 Ravi Patel: pricing: can you give us a sense Dedicated vs Private? we have a fixed budget.
07:02 Jordan Ellis: yes - high level: Dedicated is capacity-reserved with monthly commit pricing, better for predictable LLM traffic; Private is more flexible but involves setup and infra fees; we'll send a tailored pricing sheet. action: send pricing comparison.
07:14 Samir Nair: who owns OS updates and kernel patches on the private nodes?
07:18 Priya Nair: for Private, we can do two modes: managed nodes where Redwood handles updates, or we provide an installer and you run updates. For PHI-sensitive orgs customers often choose to manage the host-level patching with our guidance.
07:33 Dr. Maya Chen: can we do a short pilot with a single model in us-east-1 and a small dedicated pool?
07:40 Jordan Ellis: absolutely. typical pilot: 2-4 nodes, pinned to your region, 2-week trial for perf and regression testing. we'll instrument traces and cost breakdowns.
07:51 Elena Gomez: next - we need a technical deep dive with our Cloud Ops and Security to confirm NAT, egress IPs, and IAM roles.
07:59 Jordan Ellis: noted - we'll schedule that.
08:03 Priya Nair: quick note on artifacts - i'll drop the network diagram, port matrix, and a sample peering template (terraform) after the call.
08:12 Ravi Patel: terraform templates are helpful. do you support IAM role assumption cross-account?
08:17 Priya Nair: yes, we commonly use a cross-account role for S3/model artifact pulls and KMS decrypt.
08:24 Samir Nair: what about observability - can we get token-level cost breakdowns and per-route latency traces?
08:30 Jordan Ellis: yes, Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-route/model dashboards, tracing hooks, and export to your observability stack. we'll enable a read-only service account for your SREs.
08:44 Dr. Maya Chen: ok let's recap and set owners.
08:49 Jordan Ellis: recap: 1) Jordan to send private-deploy-guide + CIDR/port matrix + pricing; 2) Priya to prepare peering diagram and terraform sample; 3) Centauri to share VPC CIDRs, transit gateway details, egress IP constraints, and compliance checklist. Schedule deep-dive week of 2026-03-23.
09:10 Elena Gomez: agreed. thanks everyone.
09:14 Jordan Ellis: thanks all - we'll follow up with links.

End of transcript.

Shared artifacts mentioned: private-deploy-guide.pdf, benchmark-sheet.csv, sample-peering.tf (terraform), compliance-kit.zip

Call ended 15:48 UTC.
